content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E19","hypothesis_id":"H04","title":"Operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA versus TEA","purpose":"Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA in the primary P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 CO2-photoreduction formulation changes observable cobalt oxidation-state, coordination, or stability signatures during operation, and whether any donor-dependent state difference tracks catalytic output.","evidence_ids":["EV052","EV076","EV088","GX008","EV059","GX001","GX005","GX011","EV085","EV068"],"source_to_proposal":"EV059 anchors the P01 TEOA-based CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 formulation and motivates TEA as a comparator within the same family. EV052, EV076, EV088, GX008, and EV068 support operando or near-operando XAS plus complementary UV-vis/Raman/IR style characterization as a way to monitor catalyst state during CO2 reduction rather than relying only on recovered samples. GX001, GX005, and GX011 justify testing whether donor identity could alter cobalt coordination/speciation, but these are transferred from other cobalt or bipyridine-related systems and do not establish the same chemistry here. EV085 cautions that donor decomposition or decomposition-derived catalysts can confound interpretation, so signals must be treated as descriptive unless assignments are independently note that recovered-sample spectra are post-reaction references only and cannot establish the true operating state"] ,"supports":"Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference between E19G01 and E19G02 in operando or near-operando cobalt-linked observables under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the TEA and TEOA runs show different spectral evolution trajectories, coordination trends, or decay patterns that align with different CO/H2 outputs, while no-cobalt backgrounds do not explain the signal. Additional support would come from one donor showing stronger illumination-dependent change relative to its dark reference, consistent with different cobalt-manifold formation or deactivation.","refutes":"Evidence against H04 would be that E19G01 and E19G02 show indistinguishable cobalt-linked spectral features and temporal evolution within method resolution, similar dark-versus-light behavior, and similar stability trends despite reproducible catalytic CO/H2 differences established elsewhere under the same matched conditions. That would weaken cobalt-speciation/deactivation as the main explanation and shift priority toward donor photochemistry or medium effects.","inconclusive":"The result is inconclusive if cobalt signals are too weak, the suspension prevents reliable fitting, donor substitution changes optical or scattering backgrounds enough to obscure cobalt features, multiple cobalt species fit equally well, or product differences are not reproduced under the exact spectroscopic cell conditions. A donor-dependent spectral change without correlated product behavior is descriptive but not sufficient to assign catalytic relevance.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent numerical loadings or beam conditions. Use the literature-anchored P01 composition only after source verification. Pilot first to choose the lowest cobalt concentration and path length that still gives reproducible cobalt-edge signal above matrix background while preserving measurable CO/H2 formation in the spectroscopic cell. Match donor formulations by the same verified baseline recipe except donor identity. Calibrate illumination by equal reactor geometry and measured incident photon flux at the sample, then verify that both donor systems remain within a product-detection window during the spectroscopy run. If operando XAS is impractical, downgrade to near-operando rapid-transfer sampling with the same group structure and explicitly narrow claims.","limitations":"Assignments may remain ambiguous because the active cobalt species in P01 is unresolved and support-associated, solution-phase, and decomposition-derived species may coexist. Operando XAS gives element-specific state information but cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate or exclude upstream donor photochemistry as the primary cause of selectivity. UV-vis changes are non-unique and may reflect donor, ligand, support, or scattering effects. Dark-versus-light contrasts here also differ in sampling mode or elapsed state, so they are descriptive controls rather than strict single-factor causal tests. No-cobalt background is included only for the TEOA matrix, so donor-specific non-cobalt background differences may still need follow-up if TEA introduces unique interference.","feasibility":"specialist"}]}
